predecessors.name: Stem Duchy of Saxony
predecessors.text: 'Adolf I probably became the first Lord of Schauenburg in 1106'; in 1110 he 'was appointed by Lothair, Duke of Saxony to hold Holstein and Stormarn'

successors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Kassel
successors.text: the eastern territory 'continuing the name County of Schaumburg', ruled 'in personal union by Hesse-Cassel' (1640)

successors.name: County of Schaumburg-Lippe
successors.text: 'the largest portion becoming the County of Schaumburg-Lippe'

successors.name: Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg
successors.text: a third part 'incorporated into the ducal Brunswick and Lunenburgian' Principality of Lüneburg

ledger.x: 1106: Adolf I becomes the first Lord of Schauenburg.
1640: the eastern portion of the county goes to Hesse-Cassel: 'the eastern territory continuing the name County of Schaumburg', ruled 'in personal union by Hesse-Cassel'.
1640: a third part is 'incorporated into the ducal Brunswick and Lunenburgian' Principality of Lüneburg (Calenberg is not named by the page).
1640: the house dies out and the county is split.

certainty.note: The page gives no area, no boundary and no dated acquisition; the 15 km circle between Rinteln, Bückeburg and Stadthagen is a stand-in for the county on the Weser.
